input.quote: Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale: The Agreement has no indemnification article: the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), while Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all assume one exists (9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5"). With no Vendor IP indemnity the position is walk-away and the cross-reference is broken. We insert Section 20 at the preferred level only: Vendor defence and indemnity of Customer and its Affiliates for third-party claims of IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct; a notice/control/cooperation procedure; a Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law; and the 20.5 infringement remedies needed so Section 9.3's cross-reference resolves. The fallback-level exclusions have been dropped as an unnecessary carve-back on the preferred indemnity.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend and indemnify Customer and its Affiliates against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
Customer shall indemnify Vendor against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim, allow the indemnifying party to control the defence, and provide reasonable cooperation.

If the Services or Deliverables become the subject of an infringement claim, Vendor shall procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items; if none of those remedies is reasonably available, Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the affected Services and Deliverables.
